title.narrative: Direct grant-making to media organisations in low- and middle-income countries.
Media organisations supported through use of grant funds.

target.value: Host a major global learning convening to share learnings from 'What Works' unit, including in-depth market and audience research.

actual.value: Due to rapid portfolio growth and delays in getting "What Works" Unit fully operational, global learning convening was postponed to 2025.

target.value: Complete in-depth market and audience research in two IFPIM focus countries.

actual.value: Market and audience research conducted in Mongolia; process initiated in Brazil

title.narrative: Establishment of a new and unique multilateral funding mechanism that will support, through its grant-making, the resilience of public interest media organisations in low-and middle income (all ODA-eligible) countries across Latin America, Asia, and Africa.

Deployment of grant funding directly to news outlets as well as through intermediaries, establishment of regional presence in Africa, Latin America, and Asia to develop grantee pipelines, and synthesis and dissemination of learnings to inform future grant strategies.

target.value: IFPIM successfully completing its proof-of-concept period - including the legal establishment of IFPIM as a quasi-IO, the development of its regional presences, the deployment of the allocated grant capital, and dissemination of early learnings and starting to scale to a 500-million-dollar fund.

actual.value: - Status as International Organization in France confirmed, incl. privileges and immunities central to preserving the independence, multilateral character and operating model of the fund. - Regional presence established in each of the fund's focus regions: Africa and the Middle East, Asia and the Pacific, Eastern Europe, and Latin America and the Caribbean. - The Fund has committed $23M USD in funding across 79 grants made in 26 countries. - The Fund's "What Works" team has distilled lessons across the portfolio, zeroing in on effective strategies for building economic resilience in independent media. - Launched $150 million replenishment process. The total raised since the Fund's inception is almost US $70 M.

title.narrative: Establishing IFPIM as a foundation with the privileges and benefits of an international organisation headquartered in Paris, France and the creation of organisational policies and governance structures fit to purpose.
Creation and formal adoption of legal statutes and development of infrastructure to complete core activities from within independent legal entity.

target.value: Spin-out from fiscal sponsor (RPA) complete and grant-making infrastructure developed for new independent entity.

actual.value: - At the end of 2024, The Board of the International Fund approved the Fund's Bylaws and key policies related to governance, financial management, and compliance, as well as a compensation and benefits framework in anticipation of transferring employee contracts to its Paris-based entity upon receipt of decree confirming IO status in France. Work to develop additional policies to support the Fund's standalone architecture is underway. The aim is for the spin-out process to be complete by the end of 2025. - In 2024, grant-making mechanism was trialed in preparation for the next strategic period, during which the Fund will make in the order of 100 grants per year.

target.value: French legal consultants formally engaged; statutes finalized and formally approved by the French Conseil d'Etat.

actual.value: The International Fund has engaged Winston & Strawn to advise on legal matters related to the establishment and set-up of its Paris headquarters. In November 2023, the International Fund's Statutes were formally approved by the Governments of Ghana, Moldova, and France during a ceremony that triggered the International Fund's establishment as an independent legal entity as well as the formal appointment of its independent Board. The International Fund is now moving through the formal review process to confirm its status as an international organization in France (with relevant privileges and immunities). The Conseil d'Etat's formal ruling on the International Fund's application is expected in mid-2024.
